headline: Skateboard Safety Regulations Spiral Out of Control: Elbow Pads Mandatory for All Commuters
deck: Nation Gratefully Ramps Up Bureaucracy Over Minor Collision; 17 New Rules Adopted in a Day
article:
In a jaw-dropping display of bureaucratic zeal, the National Skateboard Safety Board (NSSB) convened an emergency meeting yesterday following a minor collision on Ramp 42B in downtown Sprawlville. Consequently, 17 new regulations were hastily adopted, including the eyebrow-raising requirement that all riders don mandatory elbow pads while commuting. Safety official Ted 'Wheels' McGrath, who rode the ramp to prominence as both a skateboarder and a safety advocate, declared, "We must protect ourselves from the perils of spontaneous skateboarding!" while strapping on a bewilderingly complex arrangement of knee, elbow, and wrist pads during his presentation.

According to the NSSB's newly released report, a staggering 98% of skateboard-related injuries could have been avoided had riders adhered to the organization's recently refreshed 'Skateboard Etiquette and Ramp Navigation' pamphlet, a daunting 150 pages long, filled with diagrams and an appendix on how to not be a hazard to oneself while rolling downhill. Critics have pointed out that the pamphlet’s length might be a significant barrier to safety, with Grandma Mabel from Milltown quipping, "Back in my day, we just rolled—without all this nonsense."

As citizens around the nation strap on their newly mandated protective gear in preparation for their daily commutes, the NSSB insists these measures are both necessary and effective. In a recent town hall meeting, McGrath proclaimed, "If you don't look absurd while you skateboard, are you even skateboarding?" A heated sentiment echoed by excited teenagers, now grappling with the realization that skateboarding is not just a mode of transport but a full-blown costume party.
author: Cassandra Glidewell, Chief Ramped Correspondent

oped.title: Elbow Pads: The New National Uniform for Progress
oped.author: Bartholomew Higginbotham, Chief Safety Aficionado of the Bureau of Bureaucratic Nonsense
oped.body: In a world where skateboard commuters glide gracefully along eternal ramps, who could possibly oppose the latest decree mandating elbow pads for all? Critics decry these 17 new regulations as excessive, yet they ignore the very real threat posed by rogue hats! Yes, it is those whimsical headpieces that distract our valiant skateboarders, leading to minor collisions and, dare I say, fashion disasters. Instead of rejecting this prudent legislation, we should embrace it wholeheartedly. I propose we go further: mandatory helmets adorned with flashing lights, and a uniformed 'Skate Patrol' to ticket those who dare ride without their elbow gear! If we must endure these absurd safety measures, let us at least make our skateboard utopia as bureaucratically cumbersome as possible. After all, bureaucracy is the true glue that keeps this nation from descending into chaos—just like a good elbow pad!

classifieds.text: Skateboard elbow pads for sale! Just two days old, but I found out the hard way that my elbows don't actually meet the ground when I wipe out. Open to trades for more comfortable kneepads or a ramp-friendly couch!

Need a certified elbow pad adjuster for my daily commute! Must be able to adapt to sudden stops, minor spills, and the emotional trauma of too many safety regulations. Pay in snacks and free skateboarding lessons!

Attention all ramp users: I, a humble skateboarder, have accidentally invented the world's first elbow pad trampoline. Join me at Ramp Park tonight to test it out! It's a cushy landing for all who dare to embrace the bureaucracy!

Single skateboarder seeks fellow commuter, preferably not wrapped in protective gear. Must appreciate the thrill of a good ramp ride and have a sense of humor about bureaucratic absurdity. Bonus points if you've got spare elbow pads!

stories.headline: Skateboard Insurance Premiums Soar Following New Safety Regulations
stories.deck: Experts predict every citizen will soon need a second mortgage to cover their board.
stories.article:
In the wake of mandatory elbow pads for all skateboard commuters, local insurance companies have reported a steep rise in premiums, with coverage for basic boarding incidents now averaging $1,200 annually. Insurance agent Bruce K. Crampton remarked, 'It's only natural; in a world without stairs, we’re all one tumble away from a catastrophic elbow crisis.'

As the ‘Boarded and Bumped’ clause became the industry standard, citizens have begun forming ‘Ramp Riders’ unions to protest the rates, leading to a new brokerage firm specializing in skate-related accident insurance—no pads, no problem.

stories.headline: Local Theater Announces Stairs-Free Musical: 'Ramps of Our Lives'
stories.deck: Critics laud the seamless transitions between scenes—on wheels.
stories.article:
The Maplewood Playhouse has announced its latest production, a riveting musical called 'Ramps of Our Lives,' where each number is performed on skateboards, ensuring no one has to step up or down. Director Linda V. Glide proudly stated, 'Our actors not only deliver their lines, but they also deliver them while navigating a four-foot incline—it’s the future of theater!'

With the show’s elaborate set resembling a continuous loop of interlocking ramps, local residents eagerly anticipate the opening night, with some hopeful to witness the first-ever skateboard-related stage injury, touted as a 'dramatic breakthrough' in performance art.

stories.headline: Rampage of Ramp Robbers Escalates: Police Issue Skateboard Warning
stories.deck: Authorities recommend only skateboarding with trusted companions.
stories.byline: Morty T. Quick, Crime Beat Reporter
stories.article:
Residents of Breezy Hill have been rattled by a series of slippery heists, as ramp robbers are reported to be targeting vulnerable skateboarders late at night. The Breezy Hill Police Department released a statement urging commuters to skateboard in pairs, 'Because no one should have to choose between their elbow pads and their wallet.'

Local citizen and self-proclaimed 'Ramp Vigilante' Eliza H. Boardman has begun patrolling the streets with her trusty set of protective knee and elbow gear, stating, 'I’ll protect my fellow skaters, even if it means taking a tumble myself. Just don’t ask me to stop; I can’t with these pads on!'
